summary: Re-tested all iteration_3 fixes plus a short regression. Backend: 7/7 new pytest tests pass (tests/test_iter4_fixes.py). Frontend (Playwright, admin signed in via a Clerk ticket): the Scores header shows 'max 10'. Entering 15 shows the toast 'TEST UI Game: enter a whole number from 0 to 10', sends no PUT request and puts the old value back. Valid scores 9/7/5 save and update the totals. On the public leaderboard, when every total is 0 the podium is hidden and no rows get medal styling, on both /leaderboard and the home page section. When scores are above 0, the podium shows Gold/Silver/Bronze for the top 3 and those rows get the medal border. Rank 4 with 0 points stays plain.
critical_code_review_comments: The existing tests/test_admin_api.py::test_reset calls POST /admin/scores/reset, which wipes every participant's scores. Do not run it against real fest data; mark it or remove it before the event.

update_game checks max_score against participant scores before the 404 check. This is harmless but the order is unusual. set_score and update_game are also not atomic together: a score saved at the same moment as a max_score change could slip past the new limit. Low risk.
leaderboard() reads g['max_score'] directly. Any older game document saved without max_score would cause a KeyError (500). Use g.get('max_score', 100) or add a migration.
seed_data_creation: Temporary TEST games and participants were created through the API and deleted at the end by id (all deletes returned 200). 49 score_history entries made by the test admin accounts during this run (at >= 2026-11-08T08:17) were removed. No TEST participants or games remain. The 3 Clerk test users were kept.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The DB was empty (no real games or participants) at the start. The UI 'after reset' state was simulated by setting scores to 0 through the API; the real reset endpoint was not run, to protect data. UI login: python tests/mint_tickets.py, then open /sign-in?__clerk_ticket=<token>. pytest.ini adds -n, so run pytest without -p no:xdist.
